workLog.action: Verified the PR head before creating an isolated worktree
workLog.detail: git fetch then rev-parse showed origin/fix/red-main-after-merge-sweep at 7547832109568a2f6cad909653707020e1f29ffa, equal to the expected head, so no fast-forward or new-commit inspection was needed. check_pr_live_state.py returned action ACT and pr_autofix_lease.py acquired the lease before any edit.

workLog.action: Clustered the six unresolved threads before fixing any of them
workLog.detail: cluster_threads.py reported one cluster of 4 on .agents/memory/episodes/episode-2026-08-03-session-9013.json with a single shared gist, so that gist was settled once at the source rather than four times.

workLog.action: Found that the branch was measured against a stale main
workLog.detail: git merge-base put the branch at a81239d0c while origin/main had advanced to 7281a710d. The branch carried ruff_count_baseline.txt = 308 and measured 306, which is why 102 checks were green. Merging main inherited baseline 126 and reproduced issue #4538 exactly: REGRESSION. 140 violations > baseline 126 (+14).

workLog.action: Cleared the ratchet by deleting dead noqa directives, not by raising the baseline
workLog.detail: 100 of the 140 violations were RUF100, an unused noqa for a rule not enabled at that location. Removing 17 in the two files issue #4538 names plus 1 more that the zero-tolerance changed-files gate flagged in tests/validation/test_always_on_corpus_claims.py took the count to 122 <= 126. scripts/ci/ruff_count_baseline.txt is unchanged and no suppression was added.

workLog.action: Checked the reviewer's markdown diagnosis before applying the prescribed fix
workLog.detail: The claim that a backtick code span cannot contain a newline is false: gh api /markdown with mode=gfm rendered the split span as TOTAL_BUDGET_BYTES = 6600. Applied the single-line form anyway for consistency with the same constant two paragraphs later, and because MD013 is disabled so the longer line costs nothing.

workLog.action: Split the episode-metadata cluster into the half that is fixable and the half that is generator-forced
workLog.detail: Set metrics.duration_minutes to 81, measured from the episode's only real timestamps, its three commit events at 21:00:38 and 22:21:43 UTC, which match the git committer dates of 01bada7e8 and c4f99626d. merge_preserving takes a per-key max over metrics, so a --preserve regeneration keeps 81 and applying it twice is a no-op, proven by executing the function. Left the episode timestamp at midnight: merge_preserving forces it to the session date and session-log.schema.json pins session.date to a date with no time of day, so any hand-set time is reverted on the next run.

workLog.action: Measured the outdated subprocess-encoding thread rather than arguing it
workLog.detail: scripts/validation/check_subprocess_encoding.py states the house rule in its first docstring line and its fix message. The repository has 581 call sites using errors=replace and 0 using errors=backslashreplace, so the suggestion would create the only divergent site. The consumer, assert_red, tests an ASCII substring and a return code, neither of which a replacement character can affect.

nextSteps: Issue #4538 acceptance criterion 4 is still open: add a gate that blocks lowering a ratchet baseline below the count measured on the post-merge main tree. This branch meets criteria 1 through 3 only, so the PR body cites Refs #4538 rather than Fixes.
